messages:
maria: Heads up — autoscaler keeps spiking the GPU nodepool but pods aren't bin-packing. Ended up with 6 mostly empty nodes in eu-west. Anyone seen weird interplay between soft taints and preferred affinity? :thinking:

jonathan: which nodepool + taint config? any scheduler logs?

maria: pool=gpuprod-eu. Taints on nodes look like `gpu=present:NoSchedule` (weirdly injected by infra script). Pod spec scheduling bits below:
```yaml
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: kubernetes.io/hostname
          operator: In
          values:
          - gpu-node-1
          - gpu-node-2
tolerations:
- key: "gpu"
  operator: "Exists"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

jonathan: ah — hostname-based preferred affinity + GPU anti-affinity could force spread. preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution won't move pods if they land elsewhere.

kai: That hostname preference is dangerous long-term. Cluster-autoscaler will bring up nodes for pending pods, but existing pods that prefer old hostnames won't reschedule, so new nodes stay mostly empty. Also double-check toleration key/effect equality vs what the nodes actually have.

ashley: Also check if there's requiredDuringScheduling podAntiAffinity on label `sameGpuWorkload`. If required + GPUs per pod = 1, you'll get one pod per node and autoscaler scales out.

maria: we do have a required anti-affinity in the job template (to avoid colocating heavy jobs), so that's adding to the spread. Combined with hostname prefs it explains the ripple.

jonathan: can you paste `kubectl describe pod <stuck-pod>` events?

maria: Events excerpt:
`Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3m (x4 over 5m)  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 2 node(s) had taint {gpu=present:NoSchedule}: No tolerated taint, 10 Insufficient gpu`

kai: That event is two signals: some nodes show taint not tolerated by pod (toleration mismatch), and the rest lack free GPUs. Check the exact taint key/value on nodes — our infra script sometimes sets `gpu=present` vs nodes using `gpu:NoSchedule` (no equals).

ashley: Good call. Also consider switching job anti-affinity from required->preferred so we can bin-pack when capacity is tight.

maria: Proposed immediate fixes: 1) remove hostname-based preferred affinity from job templates; 2) change one anti-affinity rule to preferred; 3) ensure tolerations exactly match node taint key/effect.

jonathan: Action list:
- kai to open PR to job templates + add unit tests for scheduler behaviour
- infra to reconcile taint key formatting across images
- add autoscaler scale-down buffer for GPU pool (avoid thrash)
- add alert for unallocated GPU nodes >10m

kai: I'll take the PR and infra ticket. Will also add a short runbook section describing how hostname preferences cause scale-thin nodes.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-334 — gpu-pool-eviction-ripple (assigned to kai)

maria: thanks — ping me when PR is up and I'll review :thumbsup:

ashley: +1 on alert rule. Suggested metric: `sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) - sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) > 0` for 10m -> fire.

jonathan: add note to runbook: avoid hostname-based affinities, prefer topologySpread or soft preferred anti-affinity for GPUs.

maria: wrapping up — PR incoming. We'll monitor scale-down after changes and adjust autoscaler params if needed.
